Role Title:  Federal Budget Analyst   Role Type:  Contractor   Location:  Remote   micro1  is engaging Federal Budget Analysts to contribute to a customer's project focused on budget formulation and execution within the federal sector. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input.   Scope of Work  
 Create realistic training examples of federal budget justification materials, including narratives, exhibits, and supporting analyses. 
 Write sample responses to OMB passback with clear, well-supported analysis, and annotate the reasoning behind each choice. 
 Document mid-year reprogramming scenarios, noting which actions require higher-level approval and how they stay consistent with spend plans. 
 Build worked examples that compare actual expenditures against planned obligations, evaluate fund availability, and explain variances. 
 Walk through year-end closeout step by step, including reconciliation with accounting records and resolution of discrepancies. 
 Write guidance on funding types, budget changes, and compliance requirements, drawing on how experienced analysts advise program managers. 
 Produce templates, process walkthroughs, and annotated examples that capture how federal budget work is actually done. 
 Review AI-generated budget content for accuracy, realism, and compliance, and explain what is wrong or missing so it can be corrected. 
  Preferred Qualifications  
 5+ years of federal budget experience at about the GS-11/12 level or higher, in GS-0560, 0501, 0510, or comparable roles. 
 Experience with budget formulation, execution, and funds control. 
 Experience with OMB submissions, reprogramming, and year-end closeout. 
 Familiarity with federal accounting and budget execution systems. 
 Financial management certification (DoD FM, CGFM, or similar) a plus.

jobs.description:
At   SafetyWing  (YC W18) , we’re building a global social safety net for remote workers—simple health, insurance, and retirement products designed to replace national welfare systems. Our mission is to remove geographical borders as a barrier to equal opportunity and freedom for everyone. If we succeed, we believe this will be one of the most important tasks of our time.  🌎 About this Role   Somewhere in the world right now, a  SafetyWing  member is messaging us. Maybe they're stuck abroad and need help fast, or they're trying to understand what their plan covers. Often the first one to answer is our AI agent, built on Intercom Fin.   We're looking for an AI Support Operations Specialist to fully own the AI agent: to make it sharper, more helpful, more human, and to keep us at the front as AI support keeps changing. You’ll own how the AI Agent performs: what it resolves, how well it resolves it, and when it hands off. You’ll also measure the difference it makes for members.   👩‍💻 What you’ll do:  
  Turn our AI agent into a top performer  
 
 Make sure our AI agent always has the most up to date information about our products, by checking with our internal policy experts 
 Look at where it succeeds, hands off or misses, find the root cause and add it to our roadmap 
 Test changes before and after launch, and keep record of what changed and what it achieved 
 Spot the next opportunities to expand the AI agent into new products and more complex support journeys 
 
  Shape how it behaves  
 
 Write and refine the AI agent's guidance, tone, and handoff behavior so every answer sounds like  SafetyWing : warm, clear, and accurate 
 Build, test, and maintain procedures and Intercom workflows, and partner with Engineering when you need integrations or technical work 
 Make sure members reach a person smoothly whenever the AI agent isn't the right one to help 
 
  Stay ahead of AI support  
 
 Keep track of new Intercom capabilities and the wider AI support field 
 Separate real breakthroughs from hype, run small pilots, and recommend what we should adopt next 
 Share what you learn in a way the team can act on right away 
 
  Work with others  
 
 Turn your findings into clear, prioritized requests for knowledge owners, and coordinate the updates that improve the AI agent's answers 
 Work with Product, Engineering, and Compliance on bugs, data questions, and new capabilities. 
 Report on the AI agent's performance to Customer Care leadership 
 Build a feedback loop so anyone in Customer Care can flag an issue and see how it was resolved 
 
 
 🧪  We are looking for someone who: 
 
 
 Has configured and improved Intercom Fin, including Guidance, workflows, or Procedures, and can show the results 
 Writes responses that are clear, accurate, and human, and can tell when one isn't 
 Finds patterns in the data, gets to the root cause, tests a fix, and measures whether it worked 
 Is comfortable with technical setup and can talk through integrations and configuration confidently with engineers 
 Follows AI closely and tests new tools, but can tell hype from real value 
 Brings teams together with clear evidence and simple explanations, and follows through 
 Extra-shine if you have experience with data privacy, insurance or healthcare 
 
  😀 We like to work with people who:  
 
 Want to help build a global social safety net on the Internet 
 Think for themselves instead of copying others 
 Are willing to try new things, even with the risk of failure 
 Are intellectually curious and open to new ideas 
 Are creative and bold in the face of any problems 
 Have strong integrity and do the right thing 
 
  🧘 Benefits beyond base pay:  
 
 Fully remote work environment – work from anywhere globally 
 Our own global safety net, giving you worldwide health, income, and travel coverage 
 A minimum of four weeks of vacation per year 
 A new laptop 
 Potential to unlock equity compensation, yearly home office allowance and more! 
 
 🚀 We look forward to hearing from you!

Role Title:  Legal & Compliance Expert   Role Type:  Contractor   Location:  Remote, global   Opportunity Snapshot    Pay:  Up to $90/hour equivalent.   Time per task:  ~10 hours per task   Engagement:  Project-based — paid per approved task   Location:  Fully remote — no geographic restrictions. Strong English required (B2 minimum, C1 preferred)   Next step:  Complete the role-specific AI interview — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client   Your tasks:  Design realistic, multi-step legal and compliance tasks with objective criteria for grading the output   micro1  is engaging experienced legal and compliance practitioners to design the tasks that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain knowledge is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.  The work is to turn real legal workflows into benchmark tasks: realistic, difficult, and gradable against objective criteria. If you’ve built a review checklist, marked up a junior associate’s draft, or trained a team against a compliance standard, that’s the instinct this needs.  Scope of Work  
 Design multi-step tasks drawn from real legal and compliance work — contract review, due diligence, regulatory assessment, risk analysis — with realistic reference files and clear instructions. 
 Define objective grading criteria so two qualified reviewers would reach the same verdict on the same output. 
 Build tasks that require judgment rather than lookup: ones where the right answer depends on reading the materials correctly. 
 Create or source the supporting materials each task needs: agreements, policy documents, regulatory texts, diligence files. 
 Flag tasks that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable instead of submitting them anyway. 
 Deliver approved tasks on schedule and at the required quality level. 
  Preferred Qualifications  
 5+ years of hands-on responsibility in contract review, due diligence, regulatory compliance, or risk — direct ownership of the work, not supervisory-only or adjacent exposure. 
 Experience creating or applying structured review standards: review checklists, diligence protocols, compliance frameworks, playbooks, or training assessments. 
 Comfortable reasoning across multiple documents at once and spotting inconsistencies between them. 
 Law degree and bar admission, or equivalent compliance qualification, is a plus but not required — practitioner experience is what matters. 
 Strong English, written and spoken — B2 minimum, C1 preferred. 
 AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required. 
  How the selection process works  
 Apply and complete the screening questions 
 Complete the AI interview — this is how we showcase your expertise to the client

jobs.description:
Role Title:  Finance Research Expert   Role Type:  Contract   Location:  Remote  Required Skills:  
  Equity Research  
  FP&A  
  Corporate Finance  
  Accounting or Audit  
  Investor Relations  
  Credit Analysis  
  Opportunity Snapshot:  
   Time per task:  around 4 to 8 hours  
   Location:  Remote, worldwide  
   You’ll need:  Hands-on experience reading US SEC filings and familiarity with US GAAP  
   Your tasks:  Write finance research questions with a verified, sourced answer, and check each one against what AI models answer  
  Scope of Work:  
  You will work on questions about real US public companies. Each question points to information that sits in long filings or IR materials, or that requires comparing several of them to find the right answer.  
  Write questions that require finding a specific figure in a 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, proxy statement, earnings release or investor presentation.  
  Write questions where two documents show different numbers and the answer depends on knowing which one is correct (for example, original vs. restated figures, or adjusted vs. reported).  
  Pay attention to period and document version: the right fiscal year, the right filing, the latest amended version.  
  Test each question against current AI models and keep only the ones they answer incorrectly.  
  Rewrite questions when the wording allows more than one valid answer.  
  What we’re looking for:  
  Hands-on work with US filings in one of these backgrounds:   
  Equity research or investment analysis (sell-side or buy-side) covering US companies. Investment banking or corporate development. (M&A, equity capital markets), with experience in deal filings, prospectuses, ownership history and subsidiary structures.  
  Credit or restructuring analysis, with experience in credit agreements, bond terms and bankruptcy filings.  
  SEC reporting or audit. (Big 4 audit, corporate reporting), with experience in restatements, footnotes and how figures change across filings.  
  Corporate law or due diligence. (Securities law, KYC, investigations), with experience tracing entities, executives and related parties across records.  
  You should also be comfortable reading long filings, including footnotes and tables, and have clear written English.  
  How the selection process works:  
  Apply with your resume and a short profile.  
  Complete the finance interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with US filings and financial reporting. You don’t need to prepare or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.  
  Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.  
  Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.  
  Originally posted on  Himalayas

Job Title:  Domain Researcher, Finance (M&A)   Job Type:  Full-time  Location: Remote     The Role    Join our research team as a  Domain Researcher (DR),  where you'll help advance AI-powered financial reasoning, with a focus on Corporate Development, Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A), and strategic transactions.    We're looking for professionals with hands-on experience in corporate development, acquisition evaluation, and M&A execution who can translate real-world financial expertise into rigorous AI evaluation frameworks.    What You'll Be Doing   
  Design and develop evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and scoring methodologies for AI agents operating in corporate development and M&A workflows.  
  Create realistic test cases covering acquisition screening, valuation, financial due diligence, deal structuring, and strategic investment decisions.  
  Evaluate AI-generated financial analyses, valuation models, acquisition assessments, and investment recommendations.  
  Translate real-world M&A experience into structured datasets, research scenarios, and measurable evaluation criteria.  
  Collaborate with AI researchers, engineers, and product teams to identify model limitations and improve financial reasoning capabilities.  
  Conduct applied research and document findings to advance AI performance in corporate finance and acquisition-related tasks.  
   What We're Looking For   
  Strong professional experience in Corporate Development, M&A, Investment Banking, Private Equity, or Strategic Investments, with direct exposure to acquisition-related transactions.  
  Hands-on experience across the M&A lifecycle, including target screening, valuation, due diligence, transaction analysis, or deal execution.  
  Strong understanding of acquisition strategies, financial modeling, company valuation (DCF, comparables, precedent transactions), and strategic fit assessments.  
  Experience preparing or evaluating investment memoranda, acquisition recommendations, and transaction-related financial analyses.  
  Ability to translate complex financial workflows into structured research questions, evaluation frameworks, and measurable criteria.  
  Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across technical and non-technical teams.  
  Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Accounting, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.  
   Preferred Qualifications   
  Direct experience within an in-house Corporate Development team, particularly involving buy-side acquisitions.  
  Experience executing or supporting M&A transactions from target identification through due diligence and closing.  
  Background in technology-sector acquisitions, SaaS businesses, or strategic investments.  
  MBA, CFA, or relevant advanced financial qualifications.  
  Familiarity with AI agents, large language models, AI evaluation methodologies, or financial AI applications.  
  Proficiency with financial modeling and analytical tools such as Excel, Python, or SQL.  
   Compensation & Benefits Notice    The national pay range for this full-time position is base salary of $200,000 –$250,000. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation during the application process, reach out to .
